name_en: Ikinari dango — steamed dumpling wrapping sweet potato and sweet bean paste
summary_ja: 輪切りにしたさつまいもとあんを小麦粉の生地で包んで蒸したおやつ。「いきなり」は熊本弁で「手早く」の意で、来客時にすぐ出せる菓子として親しまれてきたという。出来たての温かいうちに食べる。
summary_en: Slices of sweet potato and sweet bean paste are wrapped in a wheat dough and steamed into a snack. "Ikinari" means "quickly" in Kumamoto dialect, said to reflect how fast it could be made for a visiting guest, best eaten warm.
source_title: いきなり団子 熊本県

name_en: Makigaki — dried persimmons layered, rolled in bamboo bark, and bound with straw rope
summary_ja: 渋柿を天日干しにした干し柿の軸を切って開き、十数個を重ねて竹の皮で包み、藁縄でぐるぐると巻き上げた保存菓子。「福をかき寄せる」の意で年末の贈答や正月の縁起物として需要があるという。
summary_en: Sun-dried persimmons are split, layered a dozen or so at a time, wrapped in bamboo bark, and bound tightly with straw rope into a keepable sweet. Its name evokes "gathering good fortune," and it is said to be sought as a year-end gift and New Year charm.

name_en: Koppa mochi — sun-dried sweet potato pounded together with steamed mochi rice
summary_ja: 輪切りにして茹でたさつまいもを天日干しにした「こっぱ」を、蒸したもち米と砂糖であわせてつく餅。米の収穫が少ない天草で保存食として各家庭でつくられ、正月用のおやつとして重宝されてきたという。
summary_en: Sweet potato is boiled, sliced, and sun-dried into "koppa," then pounded together with steamed glutinous rice and sugar into a mochi. Made at home as a keeping food in rice-poor Amakusa, it is said to have been prized as a New Year treat.
source_title: こっぱもち 熊本県

name_en: Tojiko mame — roasted soybeans bound in a sweet wheat-flour dough and steamed in bamboo bark
summary_ja: 炒った大豆を砂糖水で煮て小麦粉を加えて練り、竹の皮に包んで蒸した素朴な菓子。「甘い生地で大豆をとじこめた」ことが名の由来とされ、山鹿市菊鹿地区では年末に必ずつくられてきたという。
summary_en: Roasted soybeans are simmered in sugar water, bound with wheat flour, wrapped in bamboo bark, and steamed into a simple sweet — its name said to mean "beans sealed in sweet dough," traditionally made every year-end in Yamaga's Kikuka district.

name_en: Kumamoto yubeshi — glutinous rice pounded with miso and yuzu, steamed in bamboo bark
summary_ja: もち米に柚子と味噌、砂糖を練り込み、竹の皮に包んで蒸した餅菓子。菊池地域では兵糧が起源とされる銘菓として伝わる一方、人吉・球磨地域には柚子の器に具を詰めて干す全く別の柚餅子があるという。
summary_en: Glutinous rice is pounded with yuzu, miso, and sugar, wrapped in bamboo bark, and steamed into a mochi sweet. In Kikuchi it survives as a confection said to trace to wartime provisions, while Hitoyoshi-Kuma keeps an entirely different version, stuffed inside a hollowed yuzu and air-dried.
